title: Live Region Mutation Testing for Commercial Cyber-Physical System Development Tool Chain
problem: Bugs in Simulink can cause unexpected compiler behaviors during model compilation; existing testing methods struggle with generating data-flow-equivalent models and creating diverse block types to comprehensively test the compiler.
motivation: Simulink is the industry standard for CPS development, so compiler bugs can propagate to deployed systems affecting safety and reliability.
method: LION tests the Simulink compiler using differential testing—running the same model across different Simulink versions and comparing results to find bugs. It inserts 'store-revert' block pairs (blocks that save and immediately restore state) between existing blocks to preserve the model's data flow. It then uses MCMC sampling (a statistical method that explores many possible block combinations) to generate diverse test cases, ensuring comprehensive compiler testing.
key_novelty: The innovation is using MCMC sampling (a statistical method) to systematically generate diverse block mutations that thoroughly test the Simulink compiler while store-revert patterns maintain data flow equivalence.
contributions: Store-revert block pair insertion mechanism to ensure data flow equivalence in mutated models
MCMC-based block mutation strategy for generating diverse test blocks
Differential testing methodology for Simulink compiler bug detection
Detected 610 additional bugs vs state-of-the-art, reported 16 valid bugs in stable Simulink version

metrics.other: 610 additional bugs detected vs SOTA (SLforge, SLEMI, COMBAT); 16 valid bugs reported in stable Simulink

limitations: Abstract does not discuss false positive rate, scalability to larger Simulink models, or generalization to other CPS development tools.
primary_theme: Differential mutation testing for Simulink compiler bugs
